Gate still running and now close to its own runtime limit.

  fixture ready        11:36:52
  observed             12:01:27
  measured elapsed     24 min 35 s   against the 30-minute gate  -> 82% consumed, not finished
  worker CPU           20 min 38 s
  worker RSS           2.17 GiB (down from 2.43, so garbage collection is working)

If this crosses 30 minutes, runtime_pass is FALSE and the gate FAILS at the degenerate fixture - the configuration with q = 2, three partitions, six edges, and a singular local covariance for 84% of supports. That would be the strongest possible form of the finding on this bead: the dense local metric path does not meet the gate even where it has the least possible work to do.

If it finishes just under 30 minutes, the reading is barely better - a pass with no headroom, obtained at settings no analysis would use, and both remedies for the degeneracy multiply the dominant cost 5-6x.

Either way the conclusion for Epic 8 is the same and is already written into its acceptance: brain-scale diagonal metrics supported, dense local metrics explicitly scoped to a declared node count or support size. The identity-metric path completes the same 50k volume in 166 seconds, so this is a boundary between metric families rather than a limit of the package.

Recommend not recording a pass from this fixture as evidence that dense local metrics scale. Reporting the boundary is the more useful result and it is what the epic asked for.
